subject: Post-demo: Redwood Dedicated vs Hyperscaler GPU — proposed tests & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Taylor <alex.taylor@amazon.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 02 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: Redwood Dedicated vs Hyperscaler GPU — proposed tests & next steps

Hey Alex —

Thanks again for joining the demo this morning and for walking through Acme's latency/throughput goals. Quick recap and a proposed qualification plan so we can compare Redwood Dedicated (reserved pools) vs your hyperscaler instance approach: 

Summary of Acme goals we heard today:
- Batch inference for 2000 concurrent users, ~4 requests/sec average but 200+ qps bursts during peak minutes
- Typical prompt length: 1k tokens; occasional 8k-token long-context runs for specific workflows
- Hard 300ms p95 cold-start latency target for short prompts; acceptable warm p95 up to ~600ms for long-context runs
- Strong need for consistent capacity guarantees during marketing spikes (no noisy-neighbor risk)

Proposed side-by-side tests (we can run these in the next 10 business days):
1) Cold vs warm latency: 1000 short prompts (1k tokens) measured cold start and after 10k tokens of warm traffic
2) Long-context performance: 200 runs of 8k-token prompt (measure p50/p95 and memory behavior)
3) Sustained throughput: 30-minute sustained load at 200 qps to validate steady-state latency and tail behavior
4) Burst resilience: 10x burst (from 20qps to 200qps) to validate autoscaling/queueing and any throttling impacts
5) Failover and regional fallback: simulated AZ outage to confirm failover time and availability

What Redwood will provide for the tests:
- Dedicated tenant with pinned GPU pool and capacity reservation for the window 
- Telemetry: token-level latency/cost breakdown, trace ids, and sample logs
- Pre-configured quantization & batching profiles we recommend for Acme's workload
- A short readme + a sample payload set (attached)

Questions / asks for your side:
- Can AWS provide a similarly isolated reserved capacity (reserved instances or dedicated host) and ensure no throttling during the burst test?
- If you run the long-context 8k runs, what instance types will you propose and what memory headroom can you guarantee per-instance?
- Any procure/contract constraints we should surface up front (purchase orders, lead time for reserved capacity)?

Next steps: If you confirm availability, we can schedule an initial 2-hour test window next Wed afternoon (Mar 11). I attached the quick test plan and a sample of the telemetry we'll share.

Thanks —
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1-415-555-0112

Thanks Marissa — good summary. A couple quick clarifying points from our side before we lock the window: 

1) Reserved capacity model: we can provide Dedicated Hosts or EC2 reservation/Capacity Reservations, but point-in-time isolation varies (Dedicated Hosts provide VM-level isolation; ENI/placement groups help for network locality). We need to confirm exact instance SKU for 8k token runs (likely p4d/g5dn families for large context) — I’ll check with infra and loop back.

2) Burst behavior: our autoscaling is policy-driven; sustained 30-minute 200 qps is fine but for a 10x sub-minute spike we may enforce scaling policies that buffer rather than instantaneously add instances. We can configure faster scale policies for a trial but we need a signed PO for guaranteed capacity in production.

3) Procurement: reserved instances usually need 30 days lead time for delivery depending on account/credits/limits. If Acme is ready to commit, we can prioritize.

Couple asks: can you share the exact payload shapes and a list of model sizes you want to exercise (e.g., 7B/13B/70B)? Also share your expected token-per-second numbers so we can size instances appropriately.

I’m available this Wed 3–4pm PT for a quick call to align test runner details.

—Alex
Alex Taylor
Senior Solutions Architect, AWS

On Mon, 02 Mar 2026 at 10:15 AM Alex Taylor <alex.taylor@amazon.com> wrote:
> Thanks Marissa — good summary. A couple quick clarifying points from our side before we lock the window: 
> 
> 1) Reserved capacity model: we can provide Dedicated Hosts or EC2 reservation/Capacity Reservations, but point-in-time isolation varies ...
> 
> 2) Burst behavior: our autoscaling is policy-driven; sustained 30-minute 200 qps is fine but for a 10x sub-minute spike we may enforce scaling policies ...

Thanks for the quick response — answers below inline and a couple of notes on Redwood's differentiation so the tests target the right hypotheses.

- Payloads & models: attached sample payloads include short and long-context templates. For the initial run we suggest exercising 13B and 70B variants to show both cost and scaling behavior. Expected TPS targets: short prompts ~600 tokens -> ~250 reqs/sec per cluster for the 13B profile; long-context 8k runs are much heavier (approx 2–4 reqs/sec per GPU depending on batching). We put conservative numbers in the attachment.

- Isolation & guarantees: Redwood Dedicated is a pinned GPU pool per customer with an SLA that includes a capacity reservation and isolation from other tenants. For the tests we'll pin capacity for the window and provide end-to-end tracing so you can see queueing vs model latency. We'll also show a test where we deliberately saturate one pool to demonstrate predictable degradation (vs noisy neighbor behavior you may see on shared instances).

- Autoscale & burst handling: For Dedicated, we can pre-provision a burst buffer (warm standby instances) that can absorb minute-scale spikes with negligible queueing. That's a configurable add-on; we typically size it as a percentage of committed capacity for marketing spikes.

- Procurement timeline: understood on the AWS side. For Redwood Dedicated short-term proof-of-value we can run a scoped trial without long-term PO; production commit would use a reserved capacity contract with a 30/60/90-day ramp in most deals.

Next steps I propose:
- You confirm whether AWS can allocate Dedicated Host / reserved capacity for a Mar 11 window (2pm–4pm PT).
- Alex: share recommended instance SKUs and any limits on max instances available in our account for the trial (so we can size load generators accordingly).
- Redwood: we’ll prepare the dedicated tenant, telemetry dashboard, and the small dataset (attached).

Scheduling: link to my calendar is below; I’ll tentatively hold Wed Mar 11 14:00–16:00 PT until we confirm.

Cheers,
Marissa

Attachments: redwood-dedicated-capacity-sample.pdf
Scheduling: https://cal.example.com/marissa/30min
